messages:
Jordan: Nightly microbench flagged a perf regression for the candidate kernel set on h100-avx512. ~1.4x latency at seq=1024, batch=1 vs baseline. KV cache shows weird miss spikes during warmup. cc @alex @maria :eyes:

ci-bot: [CI] nightly-kernel-scan #178 finished. matrix=240 runs, regressions=12, hard-fails=3. attached: /artifacts/nightly/178/summary.txt

Alex: Ugh. Which kernel id specifically? can you paste the exact repro command?

Jordan: kernel id is cand-2026-03-16-07. Repro command I used:
```
./microbench --model=llama-13b --kernel=cand-2026-03-16-07 --seq-len=1024 --batch=1 --warmup=50 --iters=200 --kv-mode=sticky
```

maria: thanks. I see the CI diffs — latency regresses on seq>=512 for avx512 codepath only, avx2 & cuda paths look fine. KV cache hit-rate drops to ~80% on warmup for this kernel vs 98% baseline.

Sam: suspect kernel's prefetch layout got changed. we recently merged a layout optimization that moved stride from 64->128 for cache lines. that can smash prefetch heuristics on longseq.

Lee: posted flame graph for the run: https://internal-redwood/fg/178/cand-2026-03-16-07.shows heavy stalls in kv_lookup() around 2.1s mark.

Alex: re-run with `--kv-mode=rotate` and with `--no-prefetch` so we can isolate prefetch vs true algorithm perf. also try batch=4 to see batching interaction.

dev-bot: queued re-run: nightly-repro-1859999000: jobs=4 (b1,b4,kv-rotate,no-prefetch). will post results when done.

ci-bot: quick summary from repro job (partial): b1/no-prefetch restored baseline latency, b1/kv-rotate still regressed, b4 shows only 1.1x regression.

Jordan: that indicates prefetch/layout is culprit, batching hides some of it. action: rollback the layout tweak on candidate-branch and re-run autotune. @maria can you open a PR to revert the stride change + add a microprobe test for kv_lookup hotpath?

maria: on it. I'll add a focused microprobe that asserts kv hit-rate >=95% within first 20 iters for seq 1024 on avx512. also will add a CI gate to block candidate kernels that fail the microprobe.

Sam: optional: add a flaky-tolerant metric in harness that tracks warmup hit-rate curve (samples 0..50 iters) so we can detect warmup regressions separately from steady-state.

Lee: agreed. that warmup curve was missing from our nightly diff visualization. I'll update the harness dashboard to include it and color regressions by warmup vs steady.

Jordan: thanks all. plan: revert layout change, re-autotune, run microprobe + nightly sweep tomorrow morning. if green, promote candidate; if not, escalate to arch-review. closing thread unless new findings. :lock:
